majorFindingsBeforeEdit: The constant-width flight made the upper stair mouth too broad relative to its foot and portal, weakening depth.
Lower stair terminals and porch balustrades were visibly too low.
The canopy's lateral points were forced up to the upper main roof, making one huge slate sheet instead of a shallow canopy below a separately readable hip/eave.
The paired foreground lantern bodies and feet sat too high in the frame, with oblique light-box faces.
structuralChanges: A single stair plan owns 18 closed tread cores, 72 separate stone caps, 36 stepped flank blocks, the landing notch, rail trajectories and terminal anchors. Clear flight flares from 4.4 m at the hall to 5.65 m at the foot, with 18 equal risers and 0.444 m runs.
The main landing and porch wings stop before the second lower tread, replacing the old platform cap overlap. Side terrain follows the same rise/run datum and closes down to the earth support.
Ground paver solids are clipped at stair-foot Z 8 instead of continuing inside the flight. Their visible textures/material assets are retained.
Taller terminal posts, curved double handrails, six intermediate post stations and taller porch balustrades restore the large approach frame.

A separate shallow entrance canopy meets the main roof at its central crown. Main hip eave is 0.8 m lower with a larger curl, a slightly wider/eccentric ridge and exposed two-tier bearing rows along both shoulders.

Hero stone lantern anchors change from X ±3.6, Z 14.5, H 3.5 to X ±3.28, Z 15.25, H 3.22. Bodies gain 1.08 width/depth factor and turn 0.32 rad inward. Base supports and plant/rock clearance follow their anchors.

visualReview.sideContactCheck: Actual side view shows a contiguous flight from ground to landing, with the platform notch and stair flanks visible. No obvious flight/platform crossing is visible in this view.
